Historical Decompositions

Source: vignettes/historical-decomposition-events.Rmd
historical-decomposition-events.Rmd

Load the demonstration models

These fits contain 200 retained draws each, for illustration rather than sampling-adequacy claims. Use ?posterior_provenance for column definitions; use help(package = "bsvarPost") for offline function documentation.

library(bsvarPost)
post <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "fiscal_post_bsvar.rds",
  package = "bsvarPost", mustWork = TRUE))
post_alt <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "fiscal_post_bsvar_alt.rds",
  package = "bsvarPost", mustWork = TRUE))

Historical decompositions from bsvars and bsvarSIGNs attribute the observed values of each variable to structural shocks at each point in time. bsvarPost aggregates these contributions over selected periods, ranks the contributions of individual shocks, and compares results across model specifications.

The analysis accepts a posterior model, a PosteriorHD object, or a draw-level table of historical decompositions. Economically meaningful shock labels should reflect the identification of the model. The documentation of bsvars and bsvarSIGNs describes estimation and computation of historical decompositions. The examples below use stored posterior draws to reproduce the reported results without re-estimating the models.

Posterior draws

Whenever a plot combines multiple shocks, including a collapsed "Other" category, it also needs posterior draws. Marginal medians and interval bounds cannot be added to obtain a grouped posterior summary. Summary-table input remains supported for ungrouped displays and one-to-one shock renaming.

The non-shock baseline is computed from all shock contributions before display filtering. A decomposition total is summarized after summing its draws; displayed marginal component medians need not add up to the median total.

Event-specific analysis requires posterior draws of historical decompositions, not only pointwise posterior summaries. For a short event, pass the posterior directly to tidy_hd_event() so that aggregation can select the window before constructing a long table. Full-sample draw tables are useful when you need several custom aggregations. Obtain them with tidy_hd(draws = TRUE):

hd_draws <- tidy_hd(post, draws = TRUE)

data.frame(
  first = head(unique(as.character(hd_draws$time)), 1),
  last = tail(unique(as.character(hd_draws$time)), 1),
  draws = length(unique(hd_draws$draw))
)
#>     first last draws
#> 1 1948.25 2026   200

Each row identifies the model, variable, shock, observation, and posterior draw. Aggregation is performed separately for every draw. Posterior summaries therefore account for uncertainty in the contribution accumulated over the entire event period.

The full-sample historical decomposition provides the context for the event analysis. The figures show the main shock contributions as separate paths and as stacked contributions.

figure <- plot_hd_overlay(post, variables = "gdp", top_n = 3,
  probability = 0.90)

Full-sample GDP shock contributions in log units. Lines show marginal posterior medians; baseline, observed series and uncertainty ribbons are omitted. Component medians need not add to the median total. 

figure <- plot_hd_stacked(post, variables = "gdp", top_n = 2,
  probability = 0.90)

Full-sample GDP decomposition in log levels, retaining two contributors and combining the remainder into Other within each draw. Stacks show marginal medians, not an exact additive decomposition of posterior medians.

Grouped and summary inputs

Grouping must sum each draw before computing its interval. This recipe combines spending and taxes into a fiscal group, leaving the remaining shock in Other. A draw table contains shock contributions only, so disable the observed series and non-shock baseline; pass post instead to recover those components:

grouped_plot <- plot_hd_overlay(hd_draws, variables = "gdp", intervals = TRUE,
  shock_groups = c(gs = "Fiscal", ttr = "Fiscal"),
  collapse_other = TRUE, probability = 0.90,
  include_observed = FALSE, include_baseline = FALSE)

For ungrouped lines a summary is sufficient:

hd_summary <- tidy_hd(post, probability = 0.90)
summary_plot <- plot_hd_lines(hd_summary, variables = "gdp")

Passing hd_summary to an overlay that merges shocks, including top_n with Other, raises a draw-level-input error. Use post, a PosteriorHD array, or tidy_hd(post, draws = TRUE) instead. plot_hd_stacked() reconstructs a full decomposition internally and requires a posterior model, even when the baseline is hidden. Plots requesting an observed series also need the posterior model.

Event periods

The empirical question determines the event period. It should not be selected from the estimated ranking of shocks. The analysis should therefore:

  1. define the dates from the research question or an external chronology;
  2. match start and end to the time labels and frequency of the data; and
  3. assess sensitivity to reasonable neighbouring periods while retaining the prespecified result.

The example uses the four quarters from 1958 to 1958.75, which are present in both stored posterior samples. No particular historical interpretation is assigned to this period. Each sample contains 200 posterior draws. The economic interpretation of every shock follows from the identifying restrictions of the fitted model.

event_start <- "1958"
event_end <- "1958.75"

event <- tidy_hd_event(
  post,
  start = event_start,
  end = event_end,
  probability = 0.90
)

subset(
  event,
  variable == "gdp",
  select = c(variable, shock, event_start, event_end,
             median, lower, upper)
)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>   variable shock event_start event_end median  lower  upper
#>   <chr>    <chr> <chr>       <chr>      <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 gdp      ttr   1958        1958.75    -1.50  -7.39  5.34 
#> 2 gdp      gs    1958        1958.75    -3.20 -12.2   0.986
#> 3 gdp      gdp   1958        1958.75   -19.5  -59.2  26.3

tidy_hd_event() sums the contribution of each shock over the inclusive period for every posterior draw and then reports posterior summaries. Set draws = TRUE to retain the aggregated draws for subsequent calculations.

The largest posterior median does not establish that a shock was the dominant historical source of variation. Credible intervals describe posterior uncertainty about the aggregated contribution, while the economic meaning of the shock remains determined by the identification of the model.

Shock rankings

shock_ranking() ranks shocks within each model and variable. The example reports results for gdp.

ranking <- shock_ranking(
  post,
  start = event_start,
  end = event_end,
  variables = "gdp",
  ranking = "absolute",
  probability = 0.90
)

ranking[, c("variable", "shock", "median", "lower", "upper", "rank")]
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   variable shock median  lower  upper  rank
#>   <chr>    <chr>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <int>
#> 1 gdp      gdp   -19.5  -59.2  26.3       1
#> 2 gdp      gs     -3.20 -12.2   0.986     2
#> 3 gdp      ttr    -1.50  -7.39  5.34      3

With ranking = "absolute", shocks are ordered by the absolute posterior median of their contribution. Use ranking = "signed" when the sign is part of the estimand. In both cases, rank is based on posterior medians. Overlapping credible intervals indicate uncertainty that is not represented by this ordering.

The plot reports the sign and magnitude of each contribution and orders the bars by the absolute posterior median.

ranking_plot <- publish_bsvar_plot(
  ranking,
  family = "shock_ranking",
  preset = "paper",
  title = "GDP contributions during the selected window",
  caption = "Bars are posterior medians; uncertainty remains in the event table."
)
ranking_plot

To plot contributions without ranking, use plot_hd_event(). The more specialized plot_hd_event_share(), plot_hd_event_cumulative(), and plot_hd_event_distribution() show the composition of contributions, their accumulation within the selected period, and their posterior distributions, respectively.

Comparison across model specifications

Comparisons of lag orders or prior distributions require the same event period for every model. compare_hd_event() applies the selected period to named posterior objects and indexes the results by model specification.

event_comparison <- compare_hd_event(
  baseline = post,
  alternative = post_alt,
  start = event_start,
  end = event_end,
  probability = 0.90
)

comparison_gdp <- subset(
  event_comparison,
  variable == "gdp",
  select = c(model, shock, event_start, event_end,
             median, lower, upper)
)
comparison_gdp
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   model       shock event_start event_end  median  lower  upper
#>   <chr>       <chr> <chr>       <chr>       <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 baseline    ttr   1958        1958.75    -1.50   -7.39  5.34 
#> 2 baseline    gs    1958        1958.75    -3.20  -12.2   0.986
#> 3 baseline    gdp   1958        1958.75   -19.5   -59.2  26.3  
#> 4 alternative ttr   1958        1958.75    -1.30   -7.96  3.93 
#> 5 alternative gs    1958        1958.75     0.169  -5.05  3.99 
#> 6 alternative gdp   1958        1958.75   -16.2   -56.2  18.8

The comparison is descriptive. Similar posterior summaries across specifications provide evidence of robustness to the considered changes, but compare_hd_event() neither selects a model nor computes the posterior probability of a difference between specifications. Names such as baseline and alternative identify the specifications in tables and plots.

Tables and figures

Posterior summaries can be reported in a labelled table, while the ranking plot can be saved separately. Both outputs are standard R objects and can be formatted for the intended application.

as_kable(
  comparison_gdp,
  caption = "GDP shock contributions in the selected event window",
  digits = 2,
  preset = "compact"
)
GDP shock contributions in the selected event window
Model Shock Event start Event end Median Lower Upper
baseline ttr 1958 1958.75 -1.50 -7.39 5.34
baseline gs 1958 1958.75 -3.20 -12.21 0.99
baseline gdp 1958 1958.75 -19.54 -59.24 26.31
alternative ttr 1958 1958.75 -1.30 -7.96 3.93
alternative gs 1958 1958.75 0.17 -5.05 3.99
alternative gdp 1958 1958.75 -16.24 -56.18 18.77 
ggplot2::ggsave(
  tempfile(fileext = ".pdf"),
  ranking_plot,
  width = 7,
  height = 4
)

For posterior summaries, response comparisons, and posterior probability statements, see Post-estimation Analysis with bsvarPost. Diagnostics for sign-restricted identification are presented in the dedicated bsvarSIGNs article.
